ja.title: 不安な場合はどのゲームをプレイすればよいですか?ボイスレコーダー VOL.761

en.title: What game should I play if I’m anxious? Voice recorder VOL.761
en.summary: [Recorder] is a member-only program launched by GPASS. The content comes from some short records of daily life and work in the computer core office. Each episode lasts about ten minutes (probably). The content may be some inappropriate thoughts, some sudden crazy remarks, or some evil person secretly recorded real daily conversations (dui ma) in the office. In short, even we ourselves don’t know who will participate in each issue and what will be recorded.

en.title: Four Hundred Years of the West Pagoda: A Micro-Global History from a Lama Pagoda to an Internet-Celebrity Food Street
en.summary: When it comes to Shenyang West Tower, many people’s first impression is a Korean style street and Korean barbecue gathering place. But few people know that the origin of this bustling consumer district is a Tibetan Buddhist lama pagoda built by Huang Taiji in the western suburbs of Shengjing City in 1643. From a Buddhist pagoda in the wilderness, to a settlement for immigrants at the intersection of railways in the colonial era, to the daily life space of ethnic minorities during the socialist construction period, it has evolved into a prosperous consumer landmark "Little Seoul" after the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and South Korea in the 21st century. In recent years, it has become an internet celebrity check-in place in the mobile Internet era - the political, economic and cultural meaning of the West Tower has been constantly rewritten by waves of forces of the times. In this episode, teacher Song Nianshen from Tsinghua University will lead us into the 380-year history of this neighborhood and rediscover the easily overlooked details of the historical changes in Northeast China, China and even East Asia in the past four centuries. en.title: Weird story: A bamboo grows in a pot, click, click, click.
en.summary: He is very fond of weird things, and talks about nonsense, ghost things, and new things related to games every day. Kill all Starscream! (Picture/Ronaldo) I can’t be called a loyal player of business simulation games, but there are usually a lot of plants planted in such games. Generally speaking, the gameplay in simulation management and plant-related games is to plant vegetables, flowers, and trees, water them on time, and wait a few days, and a batch of neat things will grow in the ground. In reality, I also like plants. But I don’t like planting flowers that much. This is because I can’t stand a plant that doesn’t grow well for more than half a year, just to wait for a short flowering period. In comparison, buying fresh cut flowers is much easier. I also prefer to spend dozens of dollars to buy a few bunches of peonies, put them in a vase, and watch them bloom into their most beautiful flowers within a few days, and then throw them away. Water lilies are also beautiful, but none of the water lilies I bought in recent times have bloomed. I’m not sure what’s wrong, but fresh cut flowers always give me a sense of joy.
